nodes.name: Gamba grass
nodes.desc: A tall bunchgrass of the Sudanian savanna. It forms much of the dry-season fuel that carries fires and feeds the grazers.

nodes.name: Shea tree
nodes.desc: A savanna tree whose fruit is eaten by fruit bats and baboons in GloBI records.

nodes.name: Jackalberry
nodes.desc: A large tree of riverside and savanna woodland. Its fruit is recorded as food for elephants, baboons, bats, warthogs and kob.

nodes.name: Tamarind
nodes.desc: A savanna tree with pod fruit that elephants, baboons, warthogs and fruit bats are recorded eating.

nodes.name: African bush elephant
nodes.desc: The park complex holds some of the last wild elephants in West Africa. They eat grass, bark and tree fruits, and shape woodland.

nodes.name: Hippopotamus
nodes.desc: Spends the day in river pools and grazes on land. Arly has pools visited by up to twenty hippos.

nodes.name: African buffalo
nodes.desc: A large grazing bovid and a main prey of lions in the Pendjari area. One of the most commonly recorded large herbivores here.

nodes.name: Roan antelope
nodes.desc: A large grass-eating antelope of Sudanian savanna, recorded often in the Arly area.

nodes.name: Kob
nodes.desc: A grazing antelope of floodplains and savanna. A frequent prey of lions and spotted hyenas.

nodes.name: Common warthog
nodes.desc: An omnivorous pig that grazes grass and eats fallen fruit. Lions and hyenas hunt it.

nodes.name: Olive baboon
nodes.desc: An omnivore that eats fruit, seeds and grass. Lions are recorded preying on it.

nodes.name: Straw-coloured fruit bat
nodes.desc: A migratory fruit bat that feeds on savanna tree fruit and so helps spread seeds.

nodes.name: Northwest African cheetah
nodes.desc: One of the last strongholds of this rare cheetah is the W-Arly-Pendjari complex, with only a few tens of individuals.

nodes.name: Spotted hyena
nodes.desc: Hunts antelope and buffalo and also scavenges kills. Present across the complex.

nodes.name: White-backed vulture
nodes.desc: A carrion-eating vulture recorded feeding on large carcasses from buffalo to elephant.

nodes.name: Hooded vulture
nodes.desc: A small resident vulture that scavenges carcasses of large herbivores.

nodes.name: West African lion
nodes.desc: The apex predator. An estimated several hundred lions live in the W-Arly-Pendjari complex, hunting buffalo, antelope and warthog.

nodes.name: Rainy season
nodes.desc: The summer rains drive the growth of grass and trees; annual rainfall at nearby Pendjari is about 1,100 mm.

nodes.name: Dry-season fire
nodes.desc: Savanna fires burn dry grass each dry season and keep woodland open.

nodes.name: River pools
nodes.desc: The Arly, Pendjari and Mekrou rivers and their pools hold water for animals in the dry season and feed the riverside forest.

nodes.name: Savanna soil
nodes.desc: Soil nutrients returned by decay support grass and tree growth.

nodes.name: Decomposers
nodes.desc: Fungi, termites and bacteria break down dead grass, leaves and carcasses and return nutrients to the soil.
